live.name: GOLD HARVEST
live.headline: GOLD HARVEST: a threat actor tracked under several names
live.in_short: The catalogue lists GOLD HARVEST under five other names and names three remote-access tools tied to it. No public report in this library describes its operations.

sentences.t: The catalogue record, sourced to Secureworks, tracks the actor as GOLD HARVEST.
The same record lists these aliases: Octo Tempest, Roasted 0ktapus, Scatter Swine, Scattered Spider and UNC3944.
The record lists three tools: AnyDesk, ConnectWise Control and Logmein.
No public report in this library describes its operations.

next.name: GOLD HARVEST
next.headline: GOLD HARVEST (Scattered Spider): a social-engineering crew that goes after help desks
next.in_short: GOLD HARVEST is Secureworks' name for the group also called Scattered Spider. Vendors describe a financially motivated actor that tricks IT help desks and outsourcers, and that sometimes works with ransomware crews.

sentences.t: GOLD HARVEST is the Secureworks name for a group also tracked as Scattered Spider, UNC3944, Octo Tempest, Scatter Swine and Roasted 0ktapus.
CrowdStrike describes Scattered Spider as a prolific eCrime adversary that has run financially motivated activity since early 2022.
Check Point Research says the group has been active since at least 2022. It describes the members as mostly young people, aged 19 to 22, from the US and UK.
ReliaQuest calls it a financially motivated gang associated with the hacking collective known as The Com.

Trustwave SpiderLabs reads "Scattered LAPSUS$ Hunters", a brand that appeared on Telegram in August 2025, as a situational alliance and not a formal merger. The brand borrows the names of Scattered Spider, ShinyHunters and LAPSUS$.
EclecticIQ assesses that ShinyHunters is very likely relying on members of Scattered Spider and The Com to run voice phishing attacks.
CrowdStrike says early campaigns reportedly hit customer relationship management and business-process outsourcing firms, along with telecommunications and technology companies.

Halcyon says the group compromises call centers and other outsourcing providers to reach many victims. It assesses that attacks on UK retail and US insurance likely began, at least in part, with such compromises.
ReliaQuest says about 70% of the group's targets are in technology, finance and retail trade.
Check Point says the group is broadening its scope to include aviation alongside enterprises.
Mandiant's M-Trends 2026 report says UNC3944 targets IT help desks to get around multifactor authentication.

ReliaQuest says the group relies on phishing and social engineering, including voice phishing and help-desk impersonation. It also uses the Evilginx phishing framework to bypass multifactor authentication.
Check Point lists SIM swapping and MFA fatigue, also called push bombing, among the group's tactics.
Halcyon says the group has consistently used insider recruitment. It says operators pose as IT staff and walk users through installing remote access tools such as AnyDesk or ScreenConnect.
The Secureworks catalogue record lists AnyDesk, ConnectWise Control and Logmein among the group's tools.

Halcyon says encryption is typically not the immediate goal. It describes a data-first extortion model, with ransomware as an escalation. It says the group has been linked to Akira, Play, Qilin and DragonForce payloads.
ReliaQuest says the group has alliances with ransomware operators ALPHV, RansomHub and DragonForce. Sygnia lists Scattered Spider among groups that attack VMware ESXi virtualization environments.

Rapid7 describes a 2026 intrusion that began with a Teams message from a fake IT Support account. It says this mirrors tradecraft seen in Octo Tempest-style campaigns, and does not call it a confirmed link.

BleepingComputer reports that in September 2023 the group breached MGM Resorts after impersonating an employee. It reports that over 100 VMware ESXi hypervisors were then encrypted with BlackCat ransomware.
ReliaQuest says a wave of attacks hit UK retailers including Marks & Spencer, Co-op and Harrods in May 2025. It says nothing definitive tied the incidents to Scattered Spider.
After insurer Aflac disclosed a breach in June 2025, a spokesperson could not name a group. The BleepingComputer report says the breach shows all the signs of a Scattered Spider attack.
Check Point says media reports and advisories have linked the group to airline attacks, including the July 2025 Qantas breach affecting six million customers.
ReliaQuest says the 2024 arrests of at least five alleged members did little to slow the group's partnerships.
Treat help-desk requests to reset passwords or multifactor authentication as high-risk. Verify the caller through a second channel, and review outsourced support providers' access.
